chapter: Radio color line, San Francisco and Columbia staff
title: Freddie Fisher testifies for Lee; the cost and pioneering
summary: Conductor Freddie Fisher appeared unasked to confirm hiring Lee; Lee was paid for 13 shows but felt the principle was unresolved.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts

blocks.x: Was Freddie Fisher there at the hearing?

Freddie Fisher surprised everyone. Freddie Fisher came to the Union. He was not supposed to be there, because they didn't tell him to come. But he heard about it, and he walked in, and he told -- he told them. He said, "He is the drummer that I hired. I told him that he had the job." He said, Because he had done a picture with him, and when the regular drummer didn't show, he said, "Get Lee Young for me". He said, "I said to get him, he said, he came in and he cut it, they would say, you know, he cut the music and I told him I would see him next week."
But prior to that, the guy from the union was saying that the leader has no right to hire musicians; that the contractor has to hire the musicians, so you know they

had to be groping then for something.
But anyway, the irony of it all is that it really did hurt. Freddie Fisher. It really did hurt him. I mean, his career. As far as going to bat for me, well, that was his last year in radio. He didn't have any more radio shows after that. And he'd been in it for quite some time. But I think that he put his career on the line. And they even went to MCA and the Camel people -- they all denied it; that they were not the cause of it, but the upshot was that everyone thought that it did come from the Camel Caravan people, you know?

That's all we could find, but I did get paid for the 13 shows, so the union made them pay me for the 13 shows. But you know, it's a funny thing about that type of thing -- that doesn't solve -- money doesn't mean anything at that stage. It's really the principle of it, and even though I got paid, I didn't feel as though I had won anything; the only way I would have felt as though I would have won anything was if I had been back in the band, because that's, what it was all about.
I thought that ... but that's pioneering, you know?
Any way you look at it, that is pioneering and that's just like, I guess you'd say, just like
the settlers had to go across country and try to settle this country, this is the melting pot and that's what you have to do, so some of us -- maybe that's our plight.
